summary: Quote latency degradation (p99 ~2-3s) in pricing-engine beginning ~13:20Z originated in redis-cache, not in pricing-engine. At 13:22:10Z the redis-cache primary (redis-cache-2) failed its health check ('3 consecutive PING timeouts; marking primary as down') and failover promoted an empty, resyncing replica (redis-cache-3). The dataset loss is corroborated by redis memory_pct dropping from ~70% to ~8.6% and hit_ratio collapsing from 96% to ~15% while redis CPU (~22%) and connected_clients (~310) stayed flat and evictions stayed at ~3/min. With the cache cold, market-data-service entered a 'cache miss storm', rebuilding every quote from the exchange feed (68 log events, rebuilds up to 8748ms), which is CPU-bound: market-data-service CPU rose from ~45% to ~90% and its p99 from ~40ms to ~2s, with request_rate flat at ~950 req/s. pricing-engine then exceeded its compute deadline waiting on market-data-service ('quote computation deadline exceeded: market-data-service took 5171ms', up to 8456ms), producing the user-visible 2-3s quote loads. The cache is slowly re-warming (hit_ratio recovering 15%->47%, latency declining), consistent with a refilling cold cache. No deployments or config changes to the quote path explain the event; the same redis-failover signature matches historical incident HIST-107.

ranked_hypotheses.title: Redis primary node failed and failed over to an empty (resyncing) replica, causing a cold-cache storm that CPU-saturated market-data-service
ranked_hypotheses.statement: The redis-cache primary redis-cache-2 failed its health check at 13:22:10Z; orchestration promoted replica redis-cache-3 whose dataset was empty. All cached quote keys vanished, so market-data-service suffered a cache-miss storm and rebuilt every quote from the exchange feed. That rebuild work is CPU-bound, driving market-data-service CPU to ~90% and its p99 from ~40ms to ~2s. pricing-engine, which calls market-data-service for quote data, then hit its compute deadline ('market-data-service took 5171ms', up to 8456ms), producing 2-3s quote latency across trading screens.

causal_chain.claim: redis-cache-2 primary fails health check (3 PING timeouts) -> marked down
failover promotes redis-cache-3, whose dataset is empty because it was resyncing
hit ratio collapses 96% -> 15% (cold cache) while redis CPU/clients steady -> dataset lost, not overload
market-data-service cache-miss storm: every quote rebuilt from exchange feed
rebuild work is CPU-bound -> market-data-service CPU 45% -> ~90%, p99 40ms -> ~2s
pricing-engine quote computation exceeds deadline waiting on market-data-service -> 2-3s quote latency

assumptions: redis-cache-2 was the actual primary serving market-data-service's quote keys
market-data-service is the sole/primary consumer that rebuilds quotes on cache miss
no additional control-plane change (deployment) to redis occurred that the deployment API failed to return

ranked_hypotheses.title: Capacity saturation: organic load outgrew market-data-service provisioned capacity
ranked_hypotheses.statement: A surge of quote traffic above provisioned capacity saturated market-data-service CPU, slowing quotes.
ranked_hypotheses.rejection_reason: market-data-service request_rate was flat at ~950-975 req/s throughout (F10) and pricing-engine request_rate was also flat; there was no traffic increase. CPU rose with unchanged load, which points to a change in work per request (cache-miss rebuilds), not more requests.

ranked_hypotheses.title: Bad deployment / config change to pricing-engine or market-data-service
ranked_hypotheses.statement: A code or config release introduced slow quote computation or cache-miss behavior.
ranked_hypotheses.rejection_reason: No deployments to pricing-engine or market-data-service on 2026-04-09 (F12) and zero config/feature-flag changes (F13). The only deploy (auth-service, 11:30Z) is off the quote path and precedes onset by ~2h.

facts.statement: pricing-engine p99 jumped from ~60ms to ~1700-2300ms at the 13:20 bucket and is slowly recovering.
pricing-engine errors are 'quote computation deadline exceeded: market-data-service took <n>ms' with downstream times up to 8456ms.
market-data-service p99 rose from ~40ms to ~1980ms at the same 13:20 onset.
market-data-service CPU rose from ~45% to ~90% (max 94.51%) while memory stayed ~62%.
market-data-service logged a cache-miss storm rebuilding quotes from the exchange feed (up to 8748ms per rebuild).
redis-cache hit_ratio collapsed from ~96% to 14.8% with CPU and client counts unchanged.
redis-cache memory_pct fell from ~70% to ~8.6% with evictions flat at ~3/min, indicating dataset loss not eviction.
redis-cache logged its primary redis-cache-2 failing health checks at 13:22:10Z.
redis-cache failed over to an empty replica (redis-cache-3) that was still resyncing.
market-data-service and pricing-engine request rates were flat across the incident.
market-data-service and pricing-engine error rates rose from ~0.2% to ~3-4% at onset.
No deployments or config changes to pricing-engine, market-data-service, or redis-cache; only an unrelated auth-service deploy at 11:30Z.
Historical incident HIST-107 matches: redis primary failure promoted an empty replica causing a cache miss storm.

assumptions: redis-cache-2 was the primary node backing market-data-service's quote cache.
market-data-service is the primary participant in the quote cache-miss rebuild path.
No control-plane change to redis occurred that a successful deployment query would have surfaced (the redis deployment query timed out).

timeline.event: Baseline: pricing-engine p99 ~60ms, market-data-service p99 ~40ms, redis hit_ratio ~96%, redis memory ~70%.
redis-cache primary redis-cache-2 fails health check (3 PING timeouts) and is marked down.
market-data-service begins logging cache-miss storm, rebuilding quotes from exchange feed.
Failover promotes empty replica redis-cache-3 to primary; dataset empty.
pricing-engine begins logging quote computation deadline-exceeded against market-data-service.
redis client reconnect storm (15048 new connections in 10s); market-data-service CPU ~90%.
Latency recovering: pricing-engine p99 ~1164ms, redis hit_ratio ~47% as cache rewarm proceeds.

recommended_actions.action: Confirm redis-cache failover root cause and complete the topology repair: verify redis-cache-2 is back in sync, and if the promoted redis-cache-3 primary is stable, no further action; otherwise fail back to a fully-synced node.
recommended_actions.rationale: The failover promoted an empty replica; the system is still re-warming and exposed to a repeat loss.

recommended_actions.action: Warm the quote cache deliberately (pre-populate hot quote keys) rather than relying on organic rebuilds, to end the CPU saturation in market-data-service faster.
recommended_actions.rationale: Full-market-data CPU saturation from rebuilds is the active cause of customer-visible latency.

recommended_actions.action: Add replica sync/pre-promotion checks so failover never promotes a replica whose dataset is empty or still resyncing.
recommended_actions.rationale: HIST-107 was fixed by exactly this ('fixed replica sync checks'); the same gap recurred.

recommended_actions.action: Add a rate limiter / circuit breaker on cold-cache rebuilds in market-data-service so a cache flush cannot drive CPU to saturation and cascade to pricing-engine deadlines.
recommended_actions.rationale: Rebuild storms are CPU-bound and propagate as quote timeouts; bounding them contains blast radius.

recommended_actions.action: Add alerting on redis hit_ratio collapse and memory_pct drop (not just CPU), since the failure was invisible in CPU/clients metrics.
recommended_actions.rationale: CPU and client metrics were flat while hit_ratio and memory collapsed; detection depended on a slow customer report.

data_gaps: The all-services and redis-cache deployment queries timed out (tc-002/tc-025/tc-032), so an operator-initiated redis change (e.g., manual failover or config push) cannot be fully excluded from the deployment/config APIs; service-scoped and window-scoped config queries returned 0 changes.
The redis-cache node failure reason (why redis-cache-2 stopped answering PINGs) is not shown in the logs; only the health-check failure and failover are recorded.
No redis-cache node-level infra metrics (node health, replication lag) were available via the metrics API to independently confirm the resyncing-replica state.

findings.statement: pricing-engine p99 latency was ~60ms until 13:12 and jumped to ~1700-2300ms from the 13:20 bucket onward, then slowly declined.

pricing-engine ERROR logs are dominated by 'quote computation deadline exceeded: market-data-service took <n>ms' (72 of 73 matches), with reported downstream times up to 8456ms; first match 13:23:57Z.

refs.quote: quote computation deadline exceeded: market-data-service took 8456ms

findings.statement: market-data-service p99 latency rose from ~40ms to ~1433-1980ms in the same 13:20 bucket, tracking pricing-engine's onset.
market-data-service CPU jumped from ~45% to ~79-94.5% at the 13:20 bucket while memory stayed flat at ~62%, indicating CPU-bound work rather than a memory leak.

market-data-service logs show a 'cache miss storm: quote:<n> not in redis-cache, rebuilding from exchange feed snapshot (<n>ms)' pattern, 68 occurrences starting 13:22:25Z with rebuild durations up to 8748ms.

refs.quote: cache miss storm: quote:84685 not in redis-cache, rebuilding from exchange feed snapshot (6864ms)

findings.statement: redis-cache hit_ratio collapsed from ~96% to 14.8% in the 13:28 bucket while cpu_pct (~22%) and connected_clients (~310) were unchanged, ruling out CPU overload of redis.

redis-cache memory_pct dropped abruptly from ~70% to ~8.6% (max 74.63 at 13:20; avg 8.56 at 13:28) with evictions_per_min flat at ~3/min, indicating the dataset was lost/emptied rather than evicted under pressure.
redis-cache log at 13:22:10Z: 'node redis-cache-2 failed health check (3 consecutive PING timeouts); marking primary as down'.

refs.quote: node redis-cache-2 failed health check (3 consecutive PING timeouts); marking primary as down

findings.statement: redis-cache log at 13:22:52Z: 'failover: promoting replica redis-cache-3 to primary; dataset on new primary is empty (replica was resyncing)'.

refs.quote: failover: promoting replica redis-cache-3 to primary; dataset on new primary is empty (replica was resyncing)

findings.statement: market-data-service request_rate was stable at ~950-975 req/s across the incident, so the CPU/latency rise is not explained by increased inbound load.
market-data-service and pricing-engine error rates rose from ~0.2% to ~3% and ~4% respectively starting at the 13:20 bucket.
No deployments to pricing-engine or market-data-service on 2026-04-09; the only deployment found was auth-service v7.2.0 at 11:30Z (unrelated to the quote path).
No config/feature-flag changes for any service (0 changes) and none specifically for redis-cache in the incident window.
market-data-service restart counter stayed at 0 throughout, so its latency/CPU rise was not caused by a restart/crashloop.

Historical incident HIST-107 ('Cold cache storm after redis failover') on the same services (redis-cache, market-data-service) had root cause 'Redis primary failure promoted an empty replica' with symptom 'cache miss storm'.

refs.quote: Redis primary failure promoted an empty replica

findings.statement: A redis-cache 'client reconnect storm' pattern appears (15048 new connections in 10s at 13:30, 92851 in 10s at 13:40), consistent with clients re-establishing connections after the failover.
